gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-elbasan: Warnes draws every stroke as a rounded rod of one weight, tapering off before the ends touch. Noto Sans Elbasan comes in as a plain sans with large lowercase forms and terminals that never pinch shut.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-elymaic: Noto Sans Elymaic reads clean and modern, its apertures standing open while the ascenders barely rise past the x-height. Noto Sans Elymaic against Warnes, with its looping tubing-thin strokes, is a pairing of loud display and quiet sans-serif text.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Expressive is the first word for Warnes, whose ruler-straight, constant-width lines run wide with stretched spacing. Noto Sans Ethiopic sits beneath as a tall, sturdy sans with c terminals hanging far from the bowl.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-georgian: Noto Sans Georgian reads modern and clean, with open curves and short ascender stems on tall lowercase bodies. Warnes is the showpiece with its one-width pen line; the body font does the steady talking.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-glagolitic: Flat, stencil-like and loud: Warnes draws its strokes with no visible shift between upright and side lines, then lets Noto Sans Glagolitic take over. The sans has sturdy round letters that stay clear at small sizes.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Noto Sans Gothic has lowercase counters as big as drilled glass beads, and its round forms curve like open parentheses. Noto Sans Gothic gives Warnes, a unit-width display face with spacious tracking, a plain sans partner that keeps things readable.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Warnes has a flat, stencil-cut feel, every stroke held to a single weight and tapering before it touches. Noto Sans Grantha follows with tall, small-bowled letters, a sans-serif that never snags on a closed-up shape.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-gujarati: Thread-thin curves, all one weight: that is Warnes, stretched out and expressive with its strokes tapering before they meet. It shouts where Noto Sans Gujarati, a clean sans with open counters, simply talks.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-gondi: Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi brings lowercase strokes as tall as a thick crayon mark, with terminals cut back to leave a big gap. Warnes is the bolder act, with no pressure swells at all; the sans simply carries the text.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-gurmukhi: Warnes shows no shading from thick to thin, just spacious, stretched strokes that taper off before touching. Noto Sans Gurmukhi sits below with outward-pointing terminals, a sans that might look best a few sizes down.
